REPORT 
 
 
The Action Taken Report (ATR) of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee 
on Science and Technology, Environment, Forests and Climate Change deals with the action taken by  
the Government  on the recommendations/observations of the  Committee contained in its ‘Three 
Hundred Seventy Fifth Report’ on ‘Demands for Grants (2023 -24) of the Department of Scientific and 
Industrial Research (DSIR)’ . The Report was presented to Rajya Sabha on the 15 th March, 2023 and 
laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on the 20th March, 2023.  
2. Action Taken Note s (ATNs) ha ve been received from the Department of Scientific and 
Industrial Research (DSIR) in respect of  all the 15 recommendations/observations contained in the 
‘Three Hundred Seventy Fifth Report’ . The r eplies of the Department of Scientific and Industrial 
Research have been categorized as follows:-  
Chapter I: Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Government: 
Para Nos., 2.8, 4.5, 5.7, 5.9, 5.11, 6.5 and 7.5  
 Total recommendations – 07  
Chapter II:    Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the Government’s replies: 
Para Nos. 2.3, 2.9, 3.5, 4.4, 5.5, 5.6 and 7.4  
 Total recommendations – 07   
Chapter III: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Government 
have not been accepted by the Committee: ‘Nil’ 
Chapter IV:   Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the 
Government are still awaited:  
Para No. 3.6  
 Total recommendation- 01 
 
3. The details of the ATNs have been analyzed in the succeeding Chapters. 

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022 -23 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR 2023-24. 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
1.1 The Committee finds merit in the Department’s request for an additional budgetary allocation 
to the tune of ₹1048.26 crore, over and above the provision made in B.E. 2023 -24. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Department may seek the requisite additional allocation from the 
Ministry of Finance at the R.E. stage. Further, the Committee recommends that,  apart from re -
appropriation of CSIR internal resources to supplement CSIR -driven projects, the Department should 
explore options for more collaborations with other Departments/Ministries as well as the private 
sector, through enhanced outreach and dissemi nation of information about i ts activities and 
achievements.                  (Para 2.8 of the 375th Report) 
 
Action Taken 
1.2 Department thankfully acknowledges the Committee’s recognition towards need for an 
additional allocation to the tune of ₹1048.26 crore, over and above the provision made in B.E. 2023-24. 
As per recommendations of the Committee, Department will seek additional funds from the Ministry of 
Finance at the R.E. stage to sustain its key programmes/initiatives. 
1.3 Department will also follow the directions of the Committee regarding exploring options for 
more collaborations with other Departments/Ministries as well as the private sector through enhanced 
outreach and dissemination of information about its activities and achievements . Department has 
already started stakeholder discussions with Industry to take their views on increasing collaboration 
with them in the areas of support to in -house R&D, more Technology Transfers & Commercialization, 
and their suggestions to create a vibrant R&D ecosystem in the c ountry.  Additionally, Department 
would also like to submit that: 
 CSIR Labs have been engaged in attracting funds from other available sources including efforts 
have been made for obtaining contributions under Corporate Social Resp onsibility (CSR) f rom 
eligible Indian Corporates/Industries for undertaking R&D projects for promotion of SDGs; 
 CSIR Labs have been interacting with stakeholder Ministries such as MoEF & CC etc. to make 
them aware of capabilities of CSIR while undertaking projects in areas of mutual interest. CSIR 
Labs are also engaged with Industries and undertakes R&D projects of global 
competitiveness/national relevance; and  
 CSIR Labs have been interacting with many Industries from India and abroad to promote CSIR 
knowledge base. Many such industries are financially supporting CSIR R&D projects f or 
development of technologies/products of their interest. 

3 
 
 
COUNCIL OF SCIENTIFIC & INDUSTRIAL RESEARCH (CSIR) 
Recommendations/Observations  
1.4 The Committee is of the view that , although many new initiatives are being undertaken, a lot 
more needs to be done in order to successfully meet the challenges of the future. The Committee 
recommends that the Department should undertake meaningful initiatives to establish strong 
foundations to enable the country to become a global leader in scientific research and development. 
While sufficient allocation of funds is an obvious pre -requisite to effectively pursue this goal, the 
Committee feels that it is essential to let more private sector /industries on board to play a greater role 
in contributing to R&D in the country. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that more 
representatives of industries/companies should be motivated to partake in this endeavour, especially by 
way of capital investments.                  (Para 4.5 ibid) 
 
Action Taken 
1.5 Department sincerely acknowle dges the C ommittee’s recommendations and will follow the 
directions of the Committee. The Department has been constantly working to promote in -house R&D 
activities of t he industry through Recognition/Registration, Certification of R&D Expenditure of the 
industry for weighted tax deductions under Section 35 (2AB) of IT Act 1961 among others. It is further 
submitted that the Department understands the requirement of transl ational R&D in terms of 
collaboration with relevant industries and getting financial support for a certain portion of R&D 
expenditure from them. CSIR has been constantly working towards this goal and is taking up a lot of 
initiatives such as NMITLI, One Week One Lab, CSIR Societal Portal, iConnect, etc. Though, with 
these efforts, there has been a great response from the industrial fraternity. However, CSIR will 
continue to explore all possible dimensions to convert the industry interests to capital investm ent in 
CSIR R&D works. Department has tasked IIM Calcutta to conduct a detailed study/evaluation of the 
ongoing Fiscal Incentive Scheme of the Department and to explore the possibility of improvement of 
industrial R&D ecosystem in the country under the aeg is of DSIR. Department has also started 
stakeholder discussions on R&D (with various industrial sectors) to take their feedback and 
suggestions on the required new initiatives for strengthening of scientific and industrial research in the 
country to make it a global leader. 
 
CAPACITY BUILDING AND HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT OF CSIR 
Recommendations/Observations  
1.6 Further, the Committee takes note of the status of CSIR award schemes, which are yet to be 
declared even at the last quarter of the current finan cial year, and recommends that appropriate and 
expeditious action may be taken to complete the process.              (Para 5.7 ibid) 
 

4 
 
Action Taken 
1.7 Department will follow the directions/recommendations of the Committee. 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
1.8 The Committee observes that the figures for patent applications filed and granted and papers 
published during 2022 -23, are lower than those of the preceding year. As these are key indicators of 
the scientific and technological advancements of a country,  the Committee exhorts CSIR to intensify its 
efforts towards improving these numbers during 2023-24.              (Para 5.9 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.9 Department will follow the directions of the Committee. It is humbly submitted that CSIR is the 
only R&D orga nization filing, prosecuting and maintaining its patents In -house in India. CSIR 
centrally as well as at lab level is increasing awaren ess through webinars/workshops/ seminars related 
to importance of filing of patents, design, copyrights and other forms of  IP. CSIR is having dedicated 
IP co-ordinators in each of its laboratories helping scientists in securing of IP. IP awareness programs 
are also conducted at the lab level. CSIR through all these interventions is trying to improve its number 
of filings not only in patents but also in other forms of IP. 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
1.10 The Committee applauds the efforts made by CSIR for revenue generation, and recommends the 
Council to set targets in this regard and, accordingly, explore more avenues for h igher revenue 
generation during the next financial year.              (Para 5.11 ibid) 
 
Action Taken 
1.11 Department thankfully acknowledges the Committee’s recognition and appreciation towards 
efforts made by CSIR for revenue generation. Department will f ollow the recommendations of the 
Committee. 
 
CSIR MISSION MODE PROJECT ON ‘WASTE TO WEALTH’ 
Recommendations/Observations  
1.12 The Committee highly commends the efforts of the Department in the field of waste 
management and, in particular, is pleased to le arn about the technologies developed for converting 
various wastes to wealth. Taking cognizance of the need for a well coordinated waste management 
strategy in the country for various types of wastes, the Committee recommends that the Department 
should make concerted efforts to ensure that the Mission project on waste to wealth is implemented 
with all sincerity and in a holistic manner. Apart from sufficient budgetary allocations towards the 
project, efforts should be made to involve other stakeholders as w ell. Further, thrust should be given to 
research and development of more waste -to-wealth technologies including for electronic wastes – the 
management of which is becoming an important issue for the country.            (Para 6.5 ibid) 

5 
 
 
Action Taken 
1.13 Department thankfully acknowledges the Committee’s recognition and appreciation of 
Department’s efforts and contribution in the field of waste management.  Department will fol low the 
recommendations of the C ommittee. It is humbly submitted that a new waste -to-wealth mission is 
under formulation by CSIR and will be launched in the FY 2023 -24 to address a variety of industrial 
and other important waste management issues, including fossil fuel waste, biotic waste, metallic waste, 
non-metallic waste, and electronic waste. 
 
MISSION PROJECT ON ACTIVE PHARMACEUTICAL INGREDIENTS (APIs) 
Recommendations/Observations  
1.14 The Committee recommends that specific targets, both short term and long term, should be set 
for reducing the dependence on imported raw materials fro m around 80 per cent at present, to 30 or 
40 per cent in the next five years. To achieve this, the Committee recommends that the proposed 
Mission project should be dovetailed with the initiatives being undertaken in this area by other 
Ministries/Departments and the private sector, adequate funds should be earmarked for the purpose so 
that financial constrains do not hinder the much needed research work, and options should be explored 
for benefiting from latest emerging technologies such as Artificial Intell igence (AI), with the overall 
objective of achieving the desired outcomes within the shortest possible timeframe. The Committee 
would also like to be kept abreast of the progress made by the Department in this regard.  
          (Para 7.5 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.15 Department will follow the directions/recomm endations of the C ommittee. It is kindly 
submitted that CSIR has excellent expertise in organic synthesis, process chemistry and chemical 
engineering.  With this expertise, CSIR has developed cost -effective processes for various APIs and 
their intermediates. Such developed processes have been successfully transferred for few molecules 
like α -Lipoic acid, Azelaic Acid and Paracetamol to pharma companies for production and 
commercialization.  A pilot plant fo r paracetamol has been erected and commissioned in 2019 at NCL. 
Similarly, CSIR contributed in repurposing of drugs for COVID -19 towards affordable health care, 
which include Remdesivir, Molnupiravir, Umifenovir, Favipiravir. Favipiravir, transferred to M/s Cipla 
Ltd, Mumbai, is commercialized in the name of “CIPLENZA”.  It is also submitted that CSIR -IICT, 
Hyderabad has already established a kilo -lab facility, which shall soon be GMP accredited lab. To 
continue R&D in this important domain and direction, a  mission project on APIs is under formulation 
with primary aim to develop viable, non -infringing synthesis routes for selected APIs, based on their 
need for the country and broadly for cardiovascular, respiratory diseases and Diabetes.  CSIR efforts in  
the domain of APIs/KSMs aspire to serve the country by aiming at import substitution and contributing 
to ‘Make in India’ program. 
 

6 
 
CHAPTER – II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE 
TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022 -23 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR 2023-24. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.1 The Committee appreciates the overall satisfactory financial performance of the Department. 
At the same time,  the Committee expresses concern over the sub -optimal utilisation in respect of the 
Central Sector Schemes/Projects, as over 50 per cent of the funds allocated under this remain to be 
utilized within the remaining quarter of the current financial year. The  Committee, therefore, urges the 
Department to ensure optimal utilization of funds during the course of the financial year. In future, 
periodic monitoring preferably on quarterly basis may be undertaken to facilitate the same. 
          (Para 2.3 of the 375th Report) 
Action Taken 
2.2 Department sincerely acknowledges the Committee’s recommendation and will follow the 
directions of the Committee. Also, as advised by the Committee, the Department will undertake 
periodic monitoring on quarterly basis to ensure  optimal utilization of funds during the course of 
the financial year. Department also thankfully acknowledges the Committee’s recognition towards 
satisfactory financial performance of CSIR.  Further, NRDC, a PSE with DSIR would also do the 
needful in ensuring complete utilization of funds for its respective schemes in the CFY 2023-24. 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
2.3 The Committee underscores the criticality of timely completion of projects and, therefore, 
recommends the Department to undertake regular r eview of its financial and physical targets, in order 
to make a practical assessment of any further corrective measures which may be required to overcome 
the challenges in the way of achieving set targets.                        (Para 2.9 ibid) 
 
Action Taken 
2.4 Department duly acknowledges the observation and concern of the Committee. Department 
would like to submit that constant monitoring/review is being made in DSIR & CSIR for the ongoing 
projects against their financial and physical targets. 
2.5 It is humbly submitted that CSIR has devised a strong monitoring mechanism for its project/s 
which is as given below:  
 The project is technically evaluated by the monitoring committee which comprises domain experts 
and evaluates the projects half -yearly and also  by the Mission/Theme Director who monitors the 
project regularly.   

7 
 
 Further, to evaluate the financials of the project there is both an internal CSIR audit and a CAG 
audit; and  
 In addition to this, the coordinating lab Director reviews and monitors the p rogress on monthly 
basis and all the administrative bottlenecks faced by the project are reviewed and handled weekly 
during the Lab Strategic Group (LSG) Meeting. 
2.6 Projects supported by NRDC are also regularly reviewed and adequate assessment is made to  
ensure timely completion and in achieving set targets and milestones.  
 
CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES/PROJECTS 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
2.7 The Committee s takes note of the important initiatives undertaken through the umbrella 
schemes of the Department, and expresses its appreciation for the significant work being done through 
them. However, given the abysmal actual utilization of funds during 2022 -23 under these schemes, as 
has been pointed out at para 2.3, the Committee is constrained to observe that a be tter monitoring 
mechanism needs to be put in place to ensure an effective check on its physical and financial 
performance. Concomitantly, the Department should also indicate and quantify, to the extent possible, 
physical targets it aspires to achieve across all the schemes/sub-schemes.            (Para 3.5 ibid) 
 
Action Taken 
2.8 Department appreciates the observation of the Committee regarding fixing of targets and for 
setting up a monitoring framework. In this regard, it is informed that targets are fixed  as per the 
approved Standing Finance Committee. In addition  to this, the targets and the achievements against 
each of these targets is monitored by Niti Aayog through the Output Outcome Monitoring framework 
office. The physical targets and the a chievements in all the schemes/ sub-schemes is also monitored by 
the concerned officer heading the program divisions in the Department. CSIR & NRDC have also set 
targets for the activities to be carried out under the schemes for the year 2023 -24 and the achievement 
in terms of physical and financial performance is regularly monitored.

Recommendations/Observations  
2.9 The Committee applauds the contribution of the Department through CSIR and its network of 
laboratories in the pursuit of excellence across all sectors of scientific research and development. The 
Committee also notes that these endeavours of CSIR are well -aligned to the economic, industrial and 
social priorities of the nation, as exemplified by their conv ergence with the Government's Mission 
Programmes such as Atma Nirbhar Bharat, Make in India, Startup India, Swachh Bharat, focus on 
green growth, etc.                   (Para 4.4 ibid)

2.10 Department thankfully acknowledges the Committee’s r ecognition and appreciation towards 
Department’s contribution through CSIR and its network of laboratories in the pursuit of excellence 
across all sectors of scientific research and development including their convergence with the 
Government’s Mission Programmes. 
 
CAPACITY BUILDING AND HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT OF CSIR 
 
Recommendations/Observations  
2.11 Recognizing the criticality of human capacity building and development, the Committee 
appreciates the work being done by the CSIR towards this end. Howeve r, the Committee notes that the 
scholarships/fellowships are provided to students mostly at higher levels. Options may, therefore, be 
explored for instituting scholarships/fellowships at lower/entry levels too, such as graduation or even 
senior secondary level, in order to encourage the youth of the country to pursue science studies.

of Science and Technology under its INSPIRE Scheme  provides scholarship to schools stude nts for 
higher studies. Further, the Department of Higher Education instituted “NSP Central Sector Scheme of 
Scholarship for college and university students” for pursuing graduation, BE/B.Tech and PG.   
2.13 The sugges tion of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee for institutin g 
scholarships/fellowships by CSIR at lower /entry levels too, such as graduation or even senior 
secondary level has been noted. Department will take the suitable needful actions if budgetary 
allocations are provided by the Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure to meet the expenses 
on such scholarships.

through the CSIR -UGC National Eligibility Test (NET). Apart from JRF -NET, CSIR also offer s JRF

fellowships/scholarships, there is a need to nurture and groom young students to become future 
scientists. CSIR, with its vast chain of scientific labs and strong team of scientists, can play a major 
role in this direction. The Committee, therefore, recomm ends that the Department should also work 
towards introducing various policies and programmes to attract, harness and retain the youth in the 
field of science.                   (Para 5.6 ibid)

through its “Jigyasa” (student -scientist connect) program since 2017. The programme envisages 
opening up the national scientific facilities to school children, enabling CSIR scientific knowledge base 
and facility to be utilized by school children to develop ‘Scientific Temper’ in the young minds thereby 
attracting school children towards science. The Jigyasa program is being implemented through CSIR

on Science and Technology, Environment, Forests and Climate Change deals with the action taken by  
the Government  on the recommendations/observations of the Committee contained in its ‘Three 
Hundred Seventy Sixth Report’ on ‘Demands for Grants (2023 -24) of the Department of Science and 
Technology’. The Report was presented to Rajya Sabha on the 15 th March, 2023 and laid on the Table 
of Lok Sabha on the 20th March, 2023.  
2. Action Taken Note s (ATNs) ha ve been received from the Department of Science and 
Technology in respect of  all the 10 recommendations/observations contained in the ‘Three Hundred 
Seventy Sixth Report’. The r eplies of the Department of Science and  Technology have been 
categorized as follows:-  
Chapter I: Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Government: 
Para Nos. 2.4, 2.12 and 7.7 
 Total recommendations – 03

 Total recommendations – 06

have not been accepted by the Committee:  
Para No. 5.5

Government are still awaited: ‘Nil’

CHAPTER – I  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022 -23 (BE, RE & ACTUAL 
EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2023-24. 
Recommendations/Observations 
1.1 The Committe e duly takes note of the reason cited by the Department regarding the under -
utilization of the budgetary allocations, and the adverse affect of introduction of the new payment 
system on implementation of its various activities/projects, as also achievement  of their physical and 
financial targets. However, the Committee is constrained to observe that the ground cited by the 
Department is primarily administrative and procedural in nature. The Committee, therefore, strongly 
recommends that the matter should be  addressed with utmost urgency and the system streamlined at 
the earliest, so that no further negative impact percolates to the next financial year.  
          (Para 2.4 of the 376th Report)  
Action Taken 
1.2 The issues r elated to new payment system have  already been sorted out. Further, despite the 
adverse effect of introduction and implementation of the new payment system, Department of Science 
and Technology was able to spend  ₹ 4744.78 crore against the RE of  ₹ 4907.17 crore, which is 
96.69% of RE for FY 2022 -23, by taking various proactive initiatives and concerted monitoring of 
expenditure. However, the recommendations of Committee are noted for compliance. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
1.3 The Committee notes the overall increase in the budgetary all ocation of the Department for the 
financial year 2023 -24, and urges the Department to ensure optimal utilization of funds during this 
period. To achieve this, the Committee recommends that periodic monitoring of the progress w.r.t 
achievement of targets may be made at least on a quarterly basis.           (Para 2.12 ibid)  
Action Taken 
1.4 On basis of recommendation of the Committee, the Department has already prepared quarterly 
plan for regular and continuous monitoring for optimal utilization of allocated  funds and to ensure 
achievement of targets and the same will be followed rigorously. 
 
NATIONAL RESEARCH FOUNDATION 
Recommendations/Observations 
1.5 The Committee takes due note of the visions, objectives and purpose of creation of the National 
Research Foundation. It believes that a centrally established NRF that transparently seeds, funds, and 
coordinates research across institutions in the country - in all disciplines, in an integrated manner, 

3 
 
with a special mandate to foster research and innovation in u niversities and colleges, including inter -
disciplinary research to provide practical solutions to societal, developmental, financial, techno -
economic challenges of the nation, is a much needed overarching mechanism. The Committee 
recommends that, in the pr ocess of implementing this programme, special consideration should be 
given towards under-funded as well as new and emerging areas of research, while also keeping under -
served regions of the country in mind.                (Para 7.7 ibid)  
Action Taken 
1.6 The National Research Foundation  (NRF) is currently under the process of approval and the 
above recommendations have been noted for compliance during implementation. 
 
 

4 
 
CHAPTER – II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE 
TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022 -23 (BE, RE & ACTUAL 
EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2023-24. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.1 The Committee observes that, in fact, the Departm ent has been allocated an additional amount 
of Rs. 800.25 crore over and above its demand for the year 2023-24. This amount is more than the bare 
minimum requirement (i.e, Rs.500 crore) projected by the Department, in the event of a reduction in 
the actual budgetary provision. In view thereof, the Committee feels that the Department should be in a 
comfortable position to sustain its key programmes and even take up additional projects during the 
year without seeking any further support to augment its budget.           (Para 2.8 of the 376th Report)  
Action Taken 
2.2 The Department of Science and Technology has proposed ₹ 7132.00 crore for FY 2023 -24 
wherein no budget was sought from National Research Foundation (NRF). In the allocated budget of 
₹7932.25 crore, there is provision of ₹ 2000.00 crore for National Resear ch Foundation which is 
proposed to be created during the current fiscal year. The rest of the allocation under BE, i.e., Rs. 
5932.25 for ongoing activities of the Department, is lesser than the BE projection of Rs.7132.0 crore. 
Considering the above, the D epartment will try to work to optimize its resources for the ongoing 
activities and may request for additional allocation as part of RE allocation for 2023-24. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.3 The Committee expresses the view that administrative and proce dural matters do not become 
major reasons for hampering the planned activities of the Department in the long run. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Department should ensure due diligence in its management of 
expenditure to ensure optimal utilization for 2023-24 as well as achievement of set targets. Besides, the 
Committee desires that all efforts should be made during the year to compensate for the mediocre 
performance during the financial year 2022-23.              (Para 2.17 ibid)  
Action Taken 
2.4 The Department has taken necessary step to streamline the administrative and procedural issues 
and the same will not impact the performance of the Department in future to achieve the set targets. 
 
KEY ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE DEPARTMENT DURING 2022-23 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.5 The Committee notes the achievements of the Department across its various schemes and 
programmes during the year, and appreciates its varied contributions for furthering scientific and 

5 
 
technological progress of the country. Th e Committee desires that the Department should focus its 
resources on more projects and programmes which align with the national priorities. The Committee 
further desires that year-wise information/data pertaining to the targets and achievements in respect of 
each major head and the various programmes under them, should be maintained in a consolidated 
manner and updated whenever required, so as to enable a wholesome assessment of their performance 
across periods.                    (Para 3.2 ibid)  
Action Taken 
2.6 The Department has already initiated few steps towards optimizing its resources aligning with 
the national priorities. During recent years, the Department has introduced a new model of S&T 
equipment facility named SATHI, an independently operated facility accessible for all the stakeholders, 
including the industries and SMEs. Similarly, the VigyanJyoti programme has been initiated for 
empowering girl students in the underrepresented STEM areas. To deal with the COVID -19 pandemic, 
a dedicated programme called CAWACH was launched to support the entire value chain of innovations 
and start-ups that addresses COVID -19 challenges. The Department has been consolidating year -wise 
information/data pertaining to the targets and achievements under the programm es and shall put 
concerted efforts to strengthen the existing mechanism in the above regard.

GOVERNMENT 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022-23 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2023-24 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
 
1.1 The Committee makes note of the variation in budgetary allocations across key schemes of the 
Department and the reasons pertaining to disruption of the global supply chain. The Committee also 
makes note of the fact that Semi -Conductor Laboratory wh ich is responsible for design and 
development of crucial electronic components has been transferred to the Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology. The Committee highlights that a significant inventory of components used in 
satellites and launch vehicles are imported as they are not manufactured in India.  
        (Para 2.13 of the 377th Report) 
1.2 While the challenges to domestic manufacturing of electronic chipsets, solar panels, atomic 
clocks and other crucial components are varied, ranging f rom availability of raw material to expertise 
in design and high scale-cost effective and precise manufacturing, the Committee recommends that the 
Department should take necessary steps in maintaining an inventory of these crucial components and 
engineer the supply chain in such a manner that it remains immune to such geo-political hurdles, to the 
largest extent possible. Further, the Committee also recommends that steps be taken to achieve higher 
indigenization in production of some key components.                                                    (Para 2.14 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.3 As recommended by the Committee, the Department shall ensure the inventory of key 
components/materials required for its on -going projects/programmes to mitigate the effects of 
disruptions in supply chain in future.  
 
1.4 The Department is pursuing Indigenis ation programs for critical technologies such as 
Travelling Wave Tube Amplifiers, Electronics packaging including LTCC (Low temperature co -fired 
ceramic) & HTCC (High temperatur e co -fired ceramic) package technology for RF, Optical, and 
Digital systems, ASICs (Application Specific Integrated Circuits), detectors. In addition, currently 
imported items are published in the Procurement Live Register  (PLR) portal of ISRO website to i nvite 
Expression of Interest (EoI) from Indian Industries for indigenous development. The indigenously 
developed atomic clock has been realized and flown in recent navigation satellite (NVS-01). 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
1.5 The Committee observes that  the major scheme heads of the Department include Space 
Technology, Space applications and INSAT Satellite Systems. While, out of the total B.E. allocations of 
Rs. 12,543.91 crore - almost 75 percent have been allocated to Space Technology, the schemes Spa ce 
applications and INSAT Satellite systems have received 12 percent and 4 percent respectively.  
                                         (Para 2.16 ibid) 
1.6 The Committee observed a general downtrend in B.E. allocations to the Department. While the 
B.E. allocation in 2021-22 was at Rs. 13,949.09 crore, it has been reduced by about 10 percent to Rs. 
12,543.91 crore in B.E. 2023 -24. Further, the allocation under the Scheme head Space Technology in 
B.E. 2023-24 is also about 10 percent less as compared to B.E. 2022-23 allocations.            
                           (Para 2.19 ibid) 

3 
 
1.7 Similarly, a strong uptrend can be seen in allocation towards the Scheme Space applications 
and INSAT Satellite Systems. While B.E. allocations under the scheme Space appli cations rose from 
Rs. 1,476.85 in 2021 -22 to Rs. 1,558.95 crore in 2023 -24, the allocations under the scheme INSAT 
Satellite Systems were increased from Rs. 329.61 crore in 2021-22 to Rs. 531 crore in B.E. 2023-24. 
(Para 2.20 ibid) 
1.8 The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department be diligent in managing the 
expenditure as well as achieving the physical targets that it has set out for itself for 2023 -24. While 
ensuring that the physical targets are accomplished , the Committee would also like to r ecommend that 
the Department ensures optimum utilisation of these funds.                                             (Para 2.22 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.9 The observations of the Committee are noted.  The Department shall strive towards achieving 
the physical targets set for the FY 2023-24 while optimally utilizing the allocated budget. 
Recommendations/Observations

December 2022) is Rs. 6,968.86 crore which is more t han 6 percent of R.E. 2022 -23, the utilization of

1.11 The Committee therefore recommends that the Department should take utmost care in ensuring 
proper utilisation of funds and since underutilisation leads to reduction in allocations, the Department 
should take extra efforts to ensure optimum utilisation under the three  heads 'Space Technology’, 
'INSAT Satellite Systems' and Space Sciences’ as the COVID induced disruptions have started being 
normalised.                                                                                                                         (Para 2.27 ibid)

TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022-23 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR 2023-24 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.1 The Committee observes that the B.E. allocation to the Department for the year 2022 -23 was 
Rs. 13,700 crore which was reduced substantially by almost 23 percent to Rs. 10,530.04 crore in R.E. 
2022-23. Further, the Committee also obse rves that though the B.E. 2023 -24 allocation of the 
Department (Rs. 12,543.91 crore) is higher by about 20 percent as compared to the revised allocation 
in 2022-23, it is still lesser than the B.E. 2022-23 allocation.    (Para 2.2 of the 377th Report) 
Action Taken 
2.2 The substantial reduction in RE 2022 -23 to Rs. 10,530.04 Crore from B.E. of Rs. 13,700 Crore 
is mainly attributable to programmatic realignment of satellite and launch vehicle programmes due to 
revised mandate of the Department, global supply chain issues, shortage in semiconductors and geo -
political issues faced during the financial year. 
2.3 The allocations made in BE 2023 -24 is adequate to meet the committed liabilities and for 
funding its on -going projects and activities. Depending on the p rogress of on -going missions, R&D 
projects and facility build -up, the Department shall review the budgetary requirements and approach 
Ministry of Finance for additional funds at RE stage and through the mechanism of supplementary 
Grants. 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.4 The Committee observes that even though the budgetary allocation for B.E. 2022 -23 (about Rs. 
13,700 crore) is almost similar to that in B.E. 2021 -22 (Rs. 13,950 crore), the R.E. 20 22-23 allocation 
(about Rs. 10,500 crore) is much less as com pared to R.E. 2021-22 (about Rs. 12,600 crore). Further, 
the B.E. 2023-24 allocation of Rs. 12,543.91 crore is the least in three years. This is also suggestive of 
the fact that the Department is transitioning from a research based institution to a more co mmercially 
oriented agency with buoyant internal revenues.                                                                (Para 2.6 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.5 As per the reformed mandate and Indian Space Policy – 2023, ISRO, as the National Space 
Agency, will focus primarily on research and development of new space technologies and applications, 
and for expanding the human understanding of outer space. M/s New  Space India Limited (NSIL), as 
the Public Sector Undertaking under DOS, shall be responsible for commercializing space technologies 
and platforms created through public expenditure. 

7 
 
2.6 In pursuant to this, the projects/programmes of ISRO are being realigned to focus on 
development of cutting -edge technologies. Production activities, hitherto carried out b y ISRO, are 
being gradually transferred to NSIL.  Accordingly, the budget allocation has been made to cater to the 
present activities of ISRO. 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.7 The Committee observes that there has been a significant reduction in revised al locations for 
2022-23 under some of the crucial schemes of the Department. The Scheme -‘Semi- Cryogenic Engine

Action Taken

contracts towards supply of flight suit, crew seat, view port etc. Further, disruptions in global supply 
chain also affected the deliveries and payments for materials, space -grade components and facilities 
required for the project. The actual expenditure incurred under the project at the end of the financial 
year is Rs. 876.94 Cr which is about 82.36% of RE 2022-23 allocations. 
2.15 The allocation under Autonomous Bodies were reduced in RE 2022 -23 as one of the 
Autonomous bodies (Semi-Conductor Laboratory) has been brought under Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology (MeitY) with effect from February 2022. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.16 The Committee also observes that while the proposed B.E. allocation fo r 2023 -24 was Rs. 
13,145 crore, the Department got Rs. 12,543.91 crore allocated in B.E. 2023 -24. The Committee was 
apprised by the Department that this allocation was sufficient to run its planned activities and schemes 
during the year with efficiency and  that if need be, the Department shall reassess the fund requirement 
at R.E. stage and approach the Ministry of Finance for additional funds.                       (Para 2.12 ibid) 

9 
 
Action Taken 
2.17 The Department has adequate allocations for its projects/ programmes/ schemes in BE 2023-24. 
Depending on the progress of on -going missions, R&D projects and facility build -up, the Department 
would approach Ministry of Finance for additional funds at RE stage and through the mechanism of 
supplementary Grants. 
 
MAJOR ACHIEVEMENTS IN THE RECENT PAST 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.18 Considering the immense potential of downstream data applications across various fields of 
governance and public service delivery such as MG -NREGA, DBT, Survey and Monitoring of land, 
location based services, domestic navigation, disaster warning, etc. the Committee recommends that 
the Department collaborates with more stakeholders, service providers and data distribution platforms 
so that more people can benefit from data based service  delivery and also add to the revenue of the 
Department.                                                                                                                          (Para 3.9 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.19 Following steps have been taken by the Depar tment to ensure broad -based penetration of 
downstream services:  
(a) For greater interaction amongst various user departments, an inter-ministerial mechanism called 
Space Applications Management System (SAMS) has been established by Government, for identif ying 
the requirements of space based services, and to recommend necessary space technology interventions 
to ensure its maximal utilisation in the respective thematic domains. SAMS framework comprises of a 
Planning Committee (PC -SAMS) as its apex body and i s supported by ten theme -specific Standing 
Committees (SCs). PC -SAMS oversees the SAMS activities, provides policy guidelines and 
recommends suitable funding mechanism to realize space assets & associated ground segment, in line 
with the space sector reforms announced by the Government. 
(b) As per the Space Policy 2023, ISRO’s remote sensing data of spatial resolution >=5m is to be 
made accessible on free & open basis to all, while remote sensing data of resolution <5m is to be made 
available free of cost t o Government entities and at fair & transparent pricing to non -governmental 
users. ISRO has established a web -based data dissemination system called Bhoonidhi Geoportal for 
hassle-free dissemination of remote sensing data to the users. 
(c) Interaction with non-governmental entities and academia with reference to Earth Observation 
data utilization & applications is promoted through the IN-SPACe mechanism.  
(d) Capacity building of the stakeholders is also being carried out regularly, for enabling their 
significant involvement in the utilisation of space based inputs.  
(e) In order to provide PNT service to strategic users, Department of Space is working closely with 
the users for building robust space and ground segments and for ensuring comprehensive deploym ent 
in strategic user segment. 
(f) In transportation sector, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has mandated 
panic button and location tracking device in all public and commercial vehicles to ensure safety of 

10 
 
passengers and timely help during distress. NavIC has been identified as an essential PNT system for 
vehicle location tracking. Additionally, MoRTH is in consultation with the Department for establishing 
the overall framework of NavIC/GNSS-based tolling in the country. Indian Railways has been utilising 
NavIC and GAGAN based devices for Real -time Train Information System (RTIS). Department is in 
consultation with the stakeholders in maritime domain, including Ministry of Shipping (MoS), for 
introducing NavIC in the maritime equipments. Depa rtment had successfully demonstrated NavIC 
based vessel positioning system to MoS. Recognition of NavIC by the International Maritime 
Organisation (IMO) has been possible due to combined efforts of the Department and MoS. 
Department is in regular consultation with Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) for adoption of GAGAN 
in civilian aircrafts. Also, MoCA has recommended NavIC as the PNT system in Drone Rules 2021. 
(g) Department is working closely with the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) for 
integrating NavIC in Aadhaar enrolment devices. Department has facilitated successful conduction of 
field trials, and is providing technical expertise in finalisation of procurement specification of the 
devices.  
(h) Department is working with Department o f Consumer Affairs (DoCA) and National Physical 
Laboratory (NPL) for the implementation of country -wide IST dissemination system. Department is 
providing technical expertise and in-house developed software for building the system.  
(i) Department is in con sultation with telecom OEMs and chipset manufacturers for ensuring 
seamless adoption of NavIC in mobile handsets in the country. The interaction is facilitated by 
Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) and Department of Telecom (DoT). Industry has already 
indicated willingness and readiness for incorporating NavIC in 5G handsets.  
(j) Department has supported National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) for utilising NavIC 
as an alert dissemination system for major natural disasters like landslides, earthquak es, floods, 
avalanches, etc. Indian National Centre for Ocean Information System (INCOIS) already utilises 
NavIC to broadcast cyclones, high waves, and tsunamis alert messages for fishermen venturing into 
deep sea. 
(k) Department is engaged with the Indian  industry, startups, and academia for promoting NavIC -
based PNT ecosystem in the country. This engagement is through technology transfers, test facility 
support, startup challenges, student hackathons, and workshops. Department also works in close 
coordination with the industries in formulating various standards applicable to the PNT domain. Some 
of the standards bodies that are actively working on NavIC standards are the Bureau of Indian 
Standards (BIS), Telecom Standards Development Society (TSDSI), Telec om Engineering Centre 
(TEC), Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), Radio Technical Commission for Maritime 
Services (RTCM), International Electrotechnical Committee (IEC), and International Standards 
Organisation (ISO). 
CAPACITY BUILDING 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.20 The Committee also recommends that the Department should ensure that these opportunities 
are not limited to a few cities or a few select institutes but rather makes in -roads to the underserved 
regions of the country as well.                                          (Para 5.5 ibid) 

11 
 
Action Taken 
2.21 ISRO has been establishing R&D cells at various academic institutes in all the regions across 
the country. So far, there are 24 R&D cells instituted at premier academic institutions like IITs, NITs & 
universities. ISRO also plans to further its presence in other institutes based on the research potential 
across the lengths and breadths of the country.  
 
2.22 In addition, more than 72 NGOs/ Institutes across the country under “Space Tutor” p rogramme 
have been identified to extend technical support to promote space education and awareness amongst 
the students in STEM areas. 
 
RESOLVING IMPORT DEPENDENCIES - ACHIEVING STATE OF THE ART 
INDIGENISATION 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.23 The Committee notes that the current import dependencies in satellite systems are to the tune of 
45-50 percent and that the Department is making earnest efforts in achieving higher indigenization. 
The Committee recommends that the Department collaborates more intensel y with the Indian industry 
as well as with the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology in finding out solutions towards 
creating the support ecosystem that enables domestic manufacturing of critical electronics 
components. This shall not only save  expensive foreign reserves but also shuttle India into the orbit of 
semiconductors and related critical technologies.                                (Para 6.4 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.24 Department has taken cognizance of the recommendations of the Committee to collaborate 
more intensely with the Indian industry as well as with the Ministry of Electronics & Information 
Technology in finding out solutions towards creating the support ecosystem that enables domestic 
manufacturing of critical electronics componen ts. Towards this, some of the measures taken to reduce 
import dependency are as follows: 
(a) Department has a continuous program me for indigenis ation and has achieved success in 
indigenizing some passive electronic components as well as critical components  like processors and 
data converters in association with Semiconductor Laboratory, Chandigarh. 
(b) Indigenisation programs for critical technologies such as Travelling wave Tube Amplifiers, 
Electronics packaging including LTCC (Low temperature co -fired cer amic) & HTCC (High 
temperature co -fired ceramic) package technology for RF, Optical, and Digital systems, ASICs  
(Application Specific Integrated Circuits). 
(c) Indigenisation targeted for Electro -Optical Detectors development using indigenous design, RF 
high power GaN HEMT technology foundry development. 
(d) The imported items are published in the Procurement Live Register  (PLR) portal of ISRO 
website to invite Expression of Interest (EoI) from Indian Industries for indigenous development. 
 

12

MAJOR ACHIEVEMENTS IN THE RECENT PAST 
Recommendation/Observation 
3.1 The Committee, at this juncture, would like to reiterate its views of t he importance of making 
BHUVAN a widely adopted -widely used -commercial application. BHUVAN has the potential of 
catering to multiple stakeholders across different verticals and the Committee strongly recommends 
that the Department should explore ways throu gh strategic partnerships with the Private Sector in 
popularizing BHUVAN application. This shall not only help the subscribers of BHUVAN take data 
backed-better informed decisions but shall also act as a source of revenue for the Department.  
        (Para 3.10 ibid)

of Government Ministries/ Departments, in addition to having provisions for visualisation of satellite

3.3 Department has taken cognizance of the direction given by the Committee to explore strategic

including commercial exploitation. Steps have already been taken in this direction, such as ISRO

3.4 Further, modalities are being worked out for extending the capabilities of Bhuvan in terms of 
Geospatial Platform, Data, Decision Support Tools, Software etc. for its utilisation by wider audience

Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
3.5 While the Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Department in popularizing the 
BHUVAN application, the Committee expects tha t the Department would take concrete  steps to

The Department has also informed that ISRO has signed  a MoU with CE Info Systems. The

TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022 -23 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2023-24 
Recommendations/Observations 
2.1 The Committee observes that the B.E. allocation to the Ministry for the year 2 022-23 was Rs. 
3,030 crore which was reduced substantially by almost 19 percent to Rs. 2,478 crore in R.E. 2022 -23. 
The Committee also observes that the B.E. 2023 -24 allocation of the Department (Rs. 3,079.40 crore), 
though higher than the R.E. 2022-23 allocation, is similar to the B.E. 2022-23 allocation. 
          (Para 2.2 of the 378th Report) 
Action Taken 
2.2 It is submitted that DOE vide OM’s dated 27.03.2021, 09.03.2022, 15.03.2022, 23.03.2022 and 
02.12.2022 revised the procedure for release of funds under Central Sector Schemes (CS) and Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes (CSS) and monitoring procedure for utilization of the funds released. The critical 
components of these instructions are as under: 
 
(i)  For each Central Sector Schemes (CS), the concerned Mi nistry will designate an Autonomous 
Body as the Central Nodal Agency (CNA) to implement the scheme. 
 
(ii)  Every State Government will designate a Single Nodal Agency (SNA) for implementing each 
CSS. The SNA will open a Single Nodal Account for each CSS at the State level in a Scheduled 
Commercial Bank authorized to conduct government business by the State Government. 
 
(iii)  In the beginning of a financial year, the Ministries/ Departments will release not more than 25% 
of the amount earmarked for a State for a CSS for the financial year. Additional central share 
(not more than 25% at a time) will be released upon transfer of the stipulated State share to the 
Single Nodal Account and utilization of at least 75% of the funds released earlier (both Central 
and State share) and compliance of the conditions of previous sanction. However, this provision 
will not be applicable in case of schemes w here a different quantum of release has been 
approved by the Cabinet. 
 
(iv)  After opening of Single Nodal Account of t he scheme and before opening zero balance 
subsidiary account of IAs or assigning those drawing rights from SNA’s account, the IAs at all 
levels shall return all unspent amount lying in their accounts to the Single Nodal Account of the 
SNA. It will be the r esponsibility of the State government concerned to ensure that the entire 
unspent amount is returned by all the IAs to the Single Nodal Account of the SNA concerned. 
For this, the State Government will work out the modalities and the timelines and will wor k out 
Central and state share in the amount so available with IAs. SNA will keep a record of unspent 
balance lying in the account of IAs and the amount refunded by IAs. 
 
(v)  The State Government will transfer the Central share received in its account in t he RBI to the 
concerned SNA’s account within a period of 21 days of its receipt. The Central share shall not 
be diverted to the Personal Deposit (PD) account or any other account by the State Government. 

5 
 
Corresponding State share should be released as earl y as possible as and not later than 40 days 
of release of Central share. The funds will be maintained by the SNA in the Single Nodal 
Account of each CSS. State Governments/ SNAs/ IAs shall not transfer scheme -related funds to 
any other bank account, except for actual payments under the Scheme. 
 
(vi)  Corresponding State share in full has been credited to by the State Government to the Single 
Nodal Account of the SNA. 
(vii) The amount released in one installment shall not be more than 25% of the amount earma rked 
for the State/ UT for a CSS for the financial year 2022-23. 
 
2.3  The on boarding of state government onto the revised PFMS regime to comply with above 
mentioned new instruction took considerable time. Ministry made best efforts to sensitize the state 
governments to quickly adapt to new financial flow procedure. The efficiency of expenditure has 
picked up and it is expected that the financial flow would be more efficient in 2023-24. 
 
2.4 Further, in respect of B.E. 2023 -24, it is to mention that Rs 39.4 0 cr. is for Cost -sharing of 
launching RISAT-1B by Ministry of Earth Science under sub-head Main Secretariat of this Ministry by

(ii)  There was a substantial decrease of about 35 percent under t he sub -head Environment 
Protection, Management and Sustainable Development. 
 
(iii)  There was a drastic reduction under the National Coastal Mission from Rs. 195 crore in B.E. 
2022-23 to only Rs. 4 crore in R.E. 2022-23. 
 
Further Recommendations/Observations  
3.3 The Committee desires to know the reasons for such drastic reduction in the above 
mentioned Central Sector Schemes of the Ministry and how this reduction in the budget 
will affect the state of environment and efforts for conservation of nature in the country. 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
3.4 The Committee is perturbed to observe that a reduction of almost 30 percent has been made in 
the proposed budgetary allocations requested by the Ministry. This may hamper the activities and 
initiatives of the M inistry across the entire gamut of Environmental protection and ecology 
management, forest & wildlife conservation as well as assistance to States and UTs. This may also lead 
to restricted implementation of many initiatives of the Ministry pertaining to Cl imate Change, 
Pollution abetment and coastal development.              (Para 2.15 ibid)

allocations may hamper the activities and initiative s of the Ministry across the entire gamut of

Ministry pertaining to Climate Change, Pollution abetment and coastal development.

manner. The Committee also desires to know the four Biosphere Reserves selected under the 
pilot project alongwith other details of Integrated Management Plan. 
 
CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES IN ECOLOGICALLY SENSITIVE AREAS 
 
Recommendations/Observations 
3.12 The Committee notes the detailed procedure followed by the Ministry before giving clearances 
to construction and infrastructure projects and would like to emphasize on the fact that the role of t he 
Ministry is to strike a balance between development and environment protection. The Committee also 
believes that a one size fits all approach to environment clearance should not be followed, especially 
for the ecologically sensitive areas of the country   such as in Joshimath, Mussoorie, Dhanaulti, etc., 
which require a more meticulous approach with the only aim of furthering the environmental interests 
rather than economic interest.                                                                                           (Para 5.10 ibid)

REPORT 
The Action Taken Report (ATR) of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Science and Technology, Environment, Forests and Climate Change deals with the 
action taken by the Government on the recommendations/observations of the Committee 
contained in its ‘Three Hundred Seventy Ninth Report’ on “Demands for Grants (202 3-24) of the 
Ministry of Earth Scienc es”.  The Report was presented to Rajya Sabha on the 15th March, 2023 
and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on the 20th March, 2023. 
2. Action Taken Notes (ATNs) have been received from Ministry of Earth Sciences  (MoES) 
in respect of all the 14 recommendations/observations contained in  the ‘Three Hundred Seventy 
Ninth Report’. The replies of the Ministry of Earth Sciences have been categorized as follows:- 
Chapter I: Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the 
Government: Para Nos.:- 2.8, 2.10, 2.11 and 2.21  
 Total recommendations – 04 
Chapter II: Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government’s replies:  
  Para Nos.:- 2.9, 2.17, 2.19, 2.20, 2.22, 2.27, 3.7, 3.9, 3.10 and 4.2 
  Total recommendations – 10  
Chapter III:  Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the 
Government have not been accepted by the Committee: NIL 
Chapter IV:  Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the 
Government are still awaited: NIL 
3. The details of the ATNs have been analyzed in the succeeding Chapters.  
  

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
OVERALL BUDGETARY DETAILS FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2022-23 (BE, RE & 
ACTUAL EXPENDITURE) AND ALLOCATION FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2023-24 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.1 Not being able to procure critical components such as high power computing devices, 
research vessels and other infrastructure has led to a reduction in allocation at the R.E. 2022 -23 
stage. This reflects poorly on the Ministry’s commitments towards its obj ectives. Further, the 
Ministry’s response that most of these schemes have a long term horizon and hence any missed 
opportunities shall be compensated for in the coming years is not satisfactory. The Committee 
therefore recommends that the Ministry should t ake all necessary steps towards dissolution of 
such hurdles and ensure that the progress on its various initiatives is not compromised. 
(Para 2.8 of the 379th Report) 
Action Taken 
1.2 Noted for compliance. The annual acquisition plan under all the schemes has been 
finalized. The order for the procurement of High Performance Computing (HPC) system has been 
placed in May 2023. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.3 Chart 2 depicts the variation in Capital Expenditure and Overall Budget in B.E. & R.E. 
2022-23 and B.E.  allocations for 2023-24. The Committee observes that the Capital expenditure 
in B.E. 2022 -23 was Rs. 450 crore which was revised down by about 59 per cent to Rs. 188.65 
crore at R.E. 2022 -23 stage. The allocation for Capital expenditure in R.E. 2022 -23 w as Rs. 
188.65 crore which has been substantially increased by about 257 percent to Rs. 673.81 crore in 
B.E. 2023 -24. The Ministry, while replying to a query of the Committee submitted that the 
increased Capital allocations during B.E. 2023 -24 will be used in Procurement of HPC, 
Acquiring of Land for setting up of Advanced Marine Biology Station and Construction of NCS 
building.                                                                                                                     (Para 2.10 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.4 Noted. The order for the procurement of High Performance Computing (HPC) system has 
been placed in May 2023. The design of the NCS building has been completed and will be 
submitted to the concerned authority for approval. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.5 The Committee notes the reasons for increase in capital expenditure as well as overall 
budgetary allocation for B.E. 2023 -24 and recommends that the Ministry should take all steps 
possible in ensuring the procurement of high performance co mputing devices and other such 
infrastructure necessary for achieving the desired outcomes under the flagship schemes of the 
Ministry. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should actively pursue with the 
Department of Space to ensure timely c ompletion and launch of the INSAT 3D satellite and that 
any value added –data based services that can be made available to the general public, service 
delivery institutions, government and law enforcement, etc., shall be done with priority.  
 (Para 2.11 ibid) 
  

3 
 
Action Taken 
1.6 Noted for compliance. The order for the procurement of High Performance Computing 
(HPC) system has been placed in May 2023. The Ministry will actively pursue with the 
Department of Space to ensure timely completion and launch of the INSAT 3D satellite. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1.7 The Committee therefore strongly recommends that the Ministry should do a thorough 
analysis of the reasons and areas of improvement to ensure that t he funds available to the 
Ministry are deployed towards achievement of the physical targets set and that the flagship 
schemes of the Ministry do not lose its objective and importance due to these inordinate delays. 
Further, the requirements in terms of Com puting Capacity, vessel related equipment and other 
research related inventory should be planned and orders be placed well in advance, so that the 
crucial initiatives of the Ministry are not stalled.                                                      (Para 2.21 ibid) 
Action Taken 
1.8 Noted for compliance. The annual acquisition plan under all the schemes has been 
finalized. The order for the procurement of High Performance Computing (HPC) system has been 
placed in May 2023. 
 
  

4 
 
CHAPTER – II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT'S REPLIES 
Recommendation/Observation 
2.1 As regards B.E. 2023 -24 allocations, the Committee observes that the Ministry has been 
given Rs. 3319.88 crore for  2023-24 which is about 25 percent more than the corresponding 
allocation in 2022 -3. To understand the reason for this substantial increase, the Committee 
sought details from the Department. In a written reply, Committee was informed that that the 
increased allocation under the sub -head Secretariat is for the rental charges of about Rs.520 
crore for the INSAT 3D satellite charges to be given to Department of Space for making and 
launching the satellite.                                                                         (Para 2.9 of the 379th Report) 
Action Taken 
2.2 Noted. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.3 The Committee emboldens the fact that the role of Ministry of Earth sciences has become 
more profound in the current context of climate change as well as in acting as an enabler of the 
Blue Economy through access to the vast oceanic resources and knowledge. Further, the 
increasing number of episodes of extreme weather phenomena has further highlighted the need 
for enhanced accuracy in prediction and diss emination of weather updates. The quest for 
knowledge concealed in the Polar Regions, is not just crucial for maintaining scientific database 
but also of great interest in protecting and furthering for India’s security interests. The deep 
ocean preserves i n itself vast resources which can be boon for our country’s economic progress 
and can prove to be a substitute for many imports which cost dearly to the country’s foreign 
reserves. In this backdrop, it is of utmost importance that the tasks at hand with th e Ministry be 
executed with great vigour and efficiency.                                                                (Para 2.17 ibid) 
 
Action Taken 
2.4 The Ministry thanks the Committee for its advice. All efforts will be made during 2023 -24 
to improve the weather, climate and ocean services. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.5 The Committee observes, with dismay, that under the head ‘O -SMART’ the Ministry was 
granted Rs. 340 crore in R.E. 2022-23 against which it could spend only Rs. 143.48 crore, thereby 
achieving only 29 percent utilisation (till January 2023). Similarly under another flagship scheme 
of the Ministry –REACHOUT, a sum of Rs. 63.13 crore was allocated in R.E. 2022 -23 against 
which the Ministry could utilise only Rs. 27.43 crore or just 43 pe rcent. Deep Ocean Mission, for 
which the Ministry was granted Rs. 300 crore during R.E. 2022 -23, it is observed that the 
Ministry could spend 61 percent of the allocation i.e. Rs. 184.39 crore. Further, as against an 
R.E. allocation of Rs. 400 crore the Ministry could spend Rs. 209 crore only, about 52 percent. 
(Para 2.19 ibid)  
Action Taken 
2.6 At the end of the FY 2022 -23, the expenditure under O -SMART was Rs. 250.20 (73.59% 
of the RE) and under REACHOUT was Rs. 60.55 Cr (95.91% of RE). 
 

5 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.7 The Committee is disheartened to see such drastic under -utilisation of allocations made to 
the Ministry under all of its flagship schemes. The severe utilisation across all flagship schemes of 
the Ministry is indicative of the fact that the  Ministry has not been able to achieve its physical 
targets that it had earlier set out. Further, the Ministry’s explanation to the Committee’s concern 
on such gross under -utilisation and subsequent reduction is not reassuring and recommends the 
Ministry to ensure optimal utilisation of funds for allocation made in F.Y. 2022 -23 as well as in 
2023-24.                                                                                                                     (Para 2.20 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.8 Noted for compliance. All efforts will be made during 2023 -24 for the optimal utilization 
of funds and achieve the physical targets. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.9 The Committee would also like to emphasize that the Ministry should chart out a detailed 
action plan  on integrating with the private sector in augmenting the reach and efficacy of the 
services offered by the Ministry especially in the field of weather forecast, disaster management, 
fisheries, etc. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should ex plore the possibilities 
of manufacturing crucial equipments domestically so that the dependencies on import and 
therefore the lead time as well as the cost, may be reduced. This shall also strengthen the Indian 
industry in manufacturing high end telemetric  equipments which shall have a huge spin -off 
advantage for other sectors as well.                                                                          (Para 2.22 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.10 Noted for compliance. India Meteorological Department (IMD), under  MoES is exploring 
the possibilities of engaging Start-ups for the development of met sensors/ software/ application/ 
dissemination tools through an MoU. The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) till date 
has signed 32 technology licensing agreements with Indian industries and is in the process of few 
more agreements in the current financial year NIOT is in the process of forming a Section 8 
Company, The proposed Marine Gate Incubation Centre (MAGIC) by NIOT will be first in the 
country which will deal exclusively in the area of ocean/marine technology. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.11 The Committee notes the physical targets set in by the Ministry under its flagship Scheme 
ACROSS and acknowledges that Atmospheric modelling and observation systems are crucial for the 
country in terms of accurately predicting weather patterns not just for  the benefit of the farming 
community but also for city administration. The increasing instances of flash floods, long dry spells, 
rapid temperature change has put pressure on the city administration since they are now tasked with 
making adequate arrangeme nts for mitigation. In such a scenario, advance forecasts shall be of 
utmost importance and should enable farmers, service providers, first responders as well as the 
general public to accordingly plan and minimize inconvenience and losses.                 (Para 2.27 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.12 The Ministry thanks the Committee for its advice. All efforts will be made during 2023 -24 
to improve the weather and climate services. 
  

6 
 
DEEP OCEAN MISSION 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.13 As regards physical targets and achievement, the Committee observed that the physical 
performance of the Ministry has been extremely disheartening. The Ministry could achieve only 7 
per cent against 15 per cent physical targets proposed for Deep Ocean Surv ey and Exploration. 
The Ministry has also achieved only 5 per cent against 20 per cent physical targets proposed for 
Establishment of an Advanced Marine Station for Ocean Biology. The Committee recommends the 
Ministry to revisit its performance in terms of  realisation of physical and financial targets set 
under Deep Ocean Mission Scheme and strive hard to improve it. Steps taken in this regard may 
be intimated to the Committee. The Committee also hopes that the Ministry, with the help of its 
periodic review s of the financial and physical performance of this Scheme, will strive hard to 
achieve the targets set for the year 2023-24.                                                               (Para 3.7 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.14 The physical and financial targets  couldn’t be achieved due to effect of Pandemic in 
realization of certain components and challenges in demonstration of technologies due to ocean 
weather. All efforts will be made during 2023-24 to achieve physical and financial targets. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.15 The Committee is constrained to take serious note of the reasons provided by the Ministry 
for sub -optimal utilisation of funds and recommends the Ministry to expedite the process of 
tendering with an aim of materializing the tender in this  financial year itself. The Committee also 
expresses its concern over the missed opportunity during the year and recommends that the 
Ministry should ensure that any loss in achievements of physical targets for the year 2022 -23 is 
compensated for in 2023 -24. Further, the Ministry should take all necessary steps to ensure that 
targets set for a particular year are met in that year itself, without having to be carried over to the 
next year.                                                                                                                      (Para 3.9 ibid) 
Action Taken 
2.16 Noted for compliance. The annual acquisition plans under all the schemes have been 
finalized. All efforts will be made during 2023-24 to achieve physical and financial targets. 
Recommendation/ Observation 
2.17 Blue Economy is crucial for India’s position as the net security as well as prosperity

REPORT 
INTRODUCTION 
 The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), came into being on August 3, 1954, 
and has been engaged in the development of nuclear power technology, application of 
radiation technologies in the fields of agriculture, health care, industry and basic 
research. 
1.2  The Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) is the apex body for formulation of 
policies and direction of the programmes. The Commission implements its policies and 
programmes through the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). The programmes of 
DAE have been divided into four sectors viz. Research and Development, Industries, 
Minerals and Power Sector. 
1.3  The programmes being followed by DAE, can be briefly summed up as follows: 
 Increasing the share of nuclear power through deployment of indigenous and 
other proven technologies and also developing fast breeder reactors and thorium 
reactors with associated fuel cycle facilities; 
 Building and operation of research reactors for production of radioisotopes; 
developing radiation technology applications in the field of health care, 
agriculture and industry, cancer care, water related technology, waste 
management etc.; 
 Designing and developing advanced technologies such as accelerators, lasers, 
supercomputers, advanced materials and instrumentation and encouraging 
transfer of technology to industry; 
 Providing support to basic research in nuclear energy and related frontier areas 
of science; interaction with universities and academic institutions; supporting 
academic programmes having a bearing on DAE’s activities; and International 
co-operation in related advanced areas of research and contribution to national 
security. 
1.4 DAE’s programmes are multidisciplinary in nature. For their execution, DAE 
has evolved abroad based organizational structure comprising research centres, 
industrial units, public sector undertakings and fully aided institutions, along with 
service organizations. These organizations are engaged in research, technology 
development and commercial operations in the areas of nuclear power and associated 
technologies, radiation technologies and their applications, basic research and academic 
programmes. 
1.5 The Department is also engaged in the development of radiation technologies 
and their applications for better crop varieties, techniques for crops protection, radiation 
based post-harvest technologies, techniques for radio-diagnosis and radiotherapy of 
diseases particularly cancer, technologies for safe drinking water, better environment 
and industrial growth. 

2 
 
1.6 Over the years, the Department has been able to establish a network of 
institutions engaged in R&D as well as industrial activities and acquired expertise in all 
aspects of the nuclear fuel cycle. The first stage of the nuclear power programme is in 
commercial domain and the second stage has been launched with the ongoing 
construction of 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR). 
1.7 Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) formed in 1987, is a 
Public Sector Enterprise under the administrative control of DAE. NPCIL is responsible 
for siting, design, construction, commissioning and operation of nuclear power reactors. 
Safety is given overriding priority in all facets of nuclear power reactors. At presents, 
NPCIL is operating 22 nuclear power reactors with an installed capacity of 6780 MW.

2.5 The Committee recommends that the DAE should adopt a more robust 
approach to financial planning and forecasting by incorporating detailed risk 
assessments and contingency allocations into the initial budget estimates. The 
Committee notes that the Revised Estimates have consistently exceeded the Budget 
Estimates. The Committee therefore urges the Department to implement regular 
internal and external audits and to ensure transparent reporting of any mid-year 
adjustments, with clear justifications for deviations from the initial allocations. 
Furthermore, it is recommended that standard operating procedures for urgent 
procurement and maintenance should be established to pre-empt emergency 
expenditures, while also integrating anticipated costs for global collaborations and 
new technologies into the budgetary framework.  
2.6 The Committee expresses major concern over the substantial gap between 
the budgetary allocations and actual utilization by the DAE. In 2023-24, the actual 
expenditure of ₹35,885.93 crore was closely aligned with the RE. However, in 
2024-25, actual expenditure stood at ₹29,051.95 crore, a mere 80.34% utilization of 
BE allocations, falling significantly short of both BE and RE by nearly ₹7,500 
crore. The Committee acknowledges that the Ministry of Finance imposed a 
budgetary cut of 13.47% on the proposed RE for 2024-25 which led to reduction in 
the allocation from the projected ₹42,256.77 crore to ₹36,564.24 crore. The 
Department informed the Committee that it has sought additional funds through the 2nd 
batch of Supplementary Demand for Grants (SDG), which, if fully allocated, would 
allow the Department to incur an expenditure of up to ₹37,362 crore during the fiscal 
year. A significant portion of the additional funds requested under the SDG is 
earmarked for critical payments, including ₹1,710.43 crore for the procurement of 
nuclear fuel from M/s TVEL, Russia, ₹595.42 crore towards India's commitments to the 
International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) project, and ₹5,900 crore for 
committed liabilities of various units, aided institutions, and Public Sector Undertakings 
(PSUs) under the capital and revenue sections. 
2.7 The Committee recommends that the Department continue to streamline 
fund disbursal processes to ensure optimal utilization of allocated resources, 
particularly for multi-year atomic energy projects. The Committee also 
recommends that a more robust financial strategy be adopted, incorporating 
contingency planning to mitigate the impact of unexpected budget cuts. 
Additionally, the Committee urges the Ministry of Finance to consider the critical 
nature of the Department’s commitments, particularly those related to nuclear 
fuel procurement and international obligations, and to ensure that adequate 
funding is provided in a timely manner. The Committee urges upon the 
Department to implement these measures with immediate effect to restore the 
expenditure trajectory to match both the budget estimates and the requirements of 
multi-year projects. The Department took note of Committee’s observations and 
assured that the Department would fully utilize the allocations by the end of FY 2024-
25 and the actual expenditure would correspond with the figures for the last three years.
